items.title: A sufficiently large base field extension makes a scheme Jacobson and makes residue fields at closed points algebraic
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over a field k, the lemma asserts that for every field extension K/k of sufficiently large cardinality, the residue field at every closed point of X_K is algebraic over K and X_K is a Jacobson scheme (statement lines 2699-2710). The proof covers X by affine opens, uses the algebra base change result for Jacobson rings and the affine criterion to attach to each member U_i a cardinal kappa_i beyond which the base change U_{i,K} has both properties, takes the maximum of the finitely many cardinals, and then applies the local criterion for Jacobson schemes to conclude for X_K (proof lines 2712-2723). The statement about residue fields is inherited from the affine members (proof lines 2724-2726). The claim is H2: a compact argument whose content is the passage from the affine pieces to the global scheme, with the cardinal threshold bookkeeping written out.
